events.title: Captain James Cook Is Killed in Hawaii
events.description: During a tense confrontation at Kealakekua Bay on the Island of Hawaii, the British explorer Captain James Cook was killed by Native Hawaiians. He was on his third great Pacific voyage.
events.significance: The death of one of history's most celebrated navigators brought his final voyage to a dramatic end. It also marked a turning point in how Europeans and Pacific Islanders encountered one another.

events.title: Oregon Becomes the 33rd U.S. State
events.description: Oregon was admitted to the Union as the 33rd state. It entered as a free state on the Pacific coast just before the Civil War.
events.significance: Its admission extended the United States further along the Pacific and added to the national debate over slavery's expansion in the years before the Civil War.

events.title: Arizona Becomes the 48th State
events.description: Arizona was admitted as the 48th state. It was the last of the contiguous United States to join the Union.
events.significance: Arizona's admission completed the map of the lower 48 states.

events.title: The St. Valentine's Day Massacre
events.description: Seven people, six of them rivals of Al Capone's gang, were murdered in a garage in Chicago during the Prohibition era.
events.significance: The killings shocked the nation and became a symbol of Prohibition-era gangland violence. They increased public pressure on authorities to act against organized crime.

events.title: ENIAC, the First General-Purpose Electronic Computer, Is Unveiled
events.description: ENIAC was unveiled to the public at the University of Pennsylvania. It was the first general-purpose electronic computer.
events.significance: ENIAC showed that electronic computing could be fast and programmable. It helped begin the digital age that now shapes everyday life.
